decisions.reason: It is very close to the firm’s core airport-operations software and integration capabilities, and the firm’s own R&D and visible dedicated positioning make continued learning and improvement likely.
As an apron connectivity module it builds directly on the firm’s established integrated airside systems knowledge, so management is likely to retain it and refine it rather than exit early.

Although billing is somewhat less central than operational control, it still leverages the firm’s airport software and data integration base, so absorptive capacity argues for keeping it while it learns the market.
Monitoring apron equipment fits closely with the firm’s installed equipment experience, service business, and digitalisation path, which lowers the chance of withdrawal.
Resource management on the apron is near the firm’s existing operational optimisation offer, making it a product the firm can understand, improve, and commercialise further.
A controller safety alert service is strongly aligned with the firm’s tower and safety portfolio, and with in-house R&D the firm is well placed to assimilate feedback and keep developing it.
